mechanism_variables: Subject-specific HRV metrics (RMSSD, LF/HF ratio)
Baroreflex sensitivity (BRS) estimated via sequence method
Sympathetic/parasympathetic balance index (e.g., LFnu/HFnu)
Segment-wise residual mean and variance
Subject ID and segment ID
mechanism_builds.causal_path: Inter-subject variation in autonomic control parameters (HRV, BRS) → systematic differences in segment-wise residual distribution parameters (mean, variance, skewness) across subjects → violation of exchangeability assumption when pooling calibration residuals across subjects → coverage probability for new subject deviates from nominal level
mechanism_builds.expected_direction: Higher inter-subject coefficient of variation in autonomic parameters (e.g., RMSSD CV > 30%) predicts larger absolute coverage deviation (|empirical coverage - nominal| > 0.05) for left-one-subject-out calibration
domain_specific_boundary_conditions: Calibration set excludes target subject (leave-one-subject-out)
Segments ≥ 5 minutes for reliable HRV/BRS estimation
Autonomic parameter variability across subjects exceeds within-subject variability across segments
No subject-level covariates included in conformal predictor
measurable_outcomes: Per-subject coverage probability at nominal 90% level
Correlation between subject autonomic parameter distance from calibration pool mean and coverage deviation
Calibration set coverage vs. test subject coverage gap
Quantile-quantile plot deviation of test residuals vs. calibration residuals
mechanism_builds.mechanism_builder_notes: Mechanism requires quantifying autonomic parameters per subject per segment; testable via leave-one-subject-out conformal prediction on multi-subject physiological datasets (e.g., MESA, CAP, or wearable studies).

mechanism_variables: Electrode-skin impedance magnitude (ohms) at segment start/end
Triaxial accelerometer variance (motion artifact proxy)
Signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of PPG/ECG per segment
Segment-wise residual variance and kurtosis
Conformity score empirical quantile per segment
mechanism_builds.causal_path: Electrode impedance drift + motion artifacts → heteroscedastic, non-stationary noise process → segment-dependent residual variance and heavy-tailed distributions → calibration quantile estimated on low-noise segments underestimates required interval width for high-noise segments → systematic undercoverage on noisy segments
mechanism_builds.expected_direction: Segments in top quartile of impedance drift (>20% change) or accelerometer variance show coverage ≤ 80% at nominal 90%, while bottom quartile segments maintain ≥ 88% coverage
domain_specific_boundary_conditions: Dry-electrode wearable sensors (PPG/ECG) in free-living conditions
Motion artifacts correlated with physiological state (e.g., stress-induced movement)
Calibration segments predominantly low-noise (resting)
No artifact rejection or adaptive noise modeling in predictor
measurable_outcomes: Coverage probability stratified by impedance drift quartile
Coverage probability stratified by accelerometer variance quartile
Correlation between segment SNR and coverage deviation
Residual variance vs. artifact metrics regression slope
mechanism_builds.mechanism_builder_notes: Testable by inducing controlled impedance changes (e.g., gel drying) and motion protocols while recording reference signals; compare conformal coverage across artifact-severity strata.

mechanism_variables: Physiological state labels (sleep stage: N1/N2/N3/REM, arousal level)
State transition timestamps (from PSG or validated algorithms)
Segment-wise residual distribution parameters (mean, variance, entropy)
Sliding calibration window size (samples)
Recalibration frequency (segments between updates)
mechanism_builds.causal_path: Autonomic state transition (e.g., NREM→REM, sleep→wake) → step-change in signal dynamics (HRV complexity, RSA amplitude) → abrupt shift in residual distribution → sliding-window recalibration lag exceeds state duration → conformity score quantile miscalibrated during transition → coverage drop
mechanism_builds.expected_direction: Coverage drops ≥ 10% below nominal within 2 minutes post-transition; drop magnitude inversely proportional to (window size / state duration) ratio; coverage recovers only after window fully contains new-state samples
domain_specific_boundary_conditions: State transitions faster than calibration window (e.g., micro-arousals < 30s, window ≥ 5 min)
State labels unavailable for stratified conformal prediction
Autonomic shift magnitude alters residual variance by ≥ 2×
Continuous monitoring with ground-truth state annotations (PSG)
measurable_outcomes: Coverage as function of time since state transition (0-10 min bins)
Minimum window size achieving ≤ 5% coverage drop at transitions
Coverage drop magnitude vs. state transition type (e.g., N2→REM vs. N3→wake)
Recalibration frequency needed for nominal coverage per state
mechanism_builds.mechanism_builder_notes: Requires high-resolution state annotations; testable on sleep datasets (e.g., SHHS, MESA Sleep) with sliding-window conformal prediction and known state transitions.

mechanism_variables: Circadian phase (hours from dim-light melatonin onset, DLMO)
Ultradian phase (cycle index within 90-120 min cycles)
Core body temperature (CBT) or proxy (wrist skin temperature)
Cortisol level or proxy (time since wake)
Segment-wise residual mean, variance, and conformity score quantile
mechanism_builds.causal_path: Endogenous circadian/ultradian rhythms → periodic modulation of baseline physiology (CBT, cortisol, autonomic tone) and signal-to-noise ratio → periodic shifts in residual distribution (mean bias, variance) → fixed calibration set (single time window) fails to capture phase-dependent shifts → coverage oscillates with time-of-day
mechanism_builds.expected_direction: Coverage oscillates with circadian period (24h) and ultradian period (90-120 min); minimum coverage at circadian phases with maximal residual variance (e.g., circadian trough ~04:00-06:00) and/or maximal model bias; amplitude of coverage oscillation ≥ 5% at nominal 90%
domain_specific_boundary_conditions: Continuous monitoring ≥ 48 hours spanning multiple circadian cycles
Rhythmic variations not fully mediated by observed covariates (e.g., activity, posture)
Calibration window shorter than circadian period (e.g., 24h calibration on 7-day data)
No time-of-day or phase features in predictor or conformal framework
measurable_outcomes: Coverage probability binned by circadian phase (4-h bins relative to DLMO)
Amplitude and phase of coverage oscillation (cosinor analysis)
Correlation between residual variance and CBT/cortisol proxy
Coverage deviation when calibrating on single phase vs. all phases
mechanism_builds.mechanism_builder_notes: Testable in multi-day ambulatory studies with circadian phase markers (DLMO, CBT); compare conformal coverage across circadian bins using fixed vs. phase-stratified calibration.

mechanism_variables: Inter-rater agreement (Cohen's kappa) per segment for target annotation
Intra-rater consistency (within-rater kappa across time)
Label noise rate estimated via latent class model or adjudication
Signal quality index (SQI) per segment
Conformity score distribution parameters per segment
mechanism_builds.causal_path: Inter-rater variability + intra-rater drift → segment-dependent label noise distribution (heteroscedastic, correlated with SQI) → conformity scores computed against noisy labels reflect annotation artifacts → calibration quantile biased toward noise distribution → coverage guarantee invalid (covers noisy labels, not true state)
mechanism_builds.expected_direction: Segments with kappa < 0.7 show coverage deviation ≥ 8% from nominal; direction of deviation depends on noise asymmetry (e.g., systematic over-scoring of deep sleep → overcoverage for deep sleep, undercoverage for light sleep)
domain_specific_boundary_conditions: Physiological event labeling with known inter-rater variability (e.g., sleep staging, seizure detection)
Label noise heteroscedastic across segments (worse in low-SQI segments)
No gold-standard adjudicated labels for calibration
Conformal predictor uses raw annotations as ground truth
measurable_outcomes: Coverage vs. segment-level inter-rater kappa (binned)
Bias in conformity score quantile vs. label noise rate estimate
Coverage stratified by SQI tertiles
Difference in coverage when using adjudicated vs. single-rater labels for calibration
mechanism_builds.mechanism_builder_notes: Requires multi-rater annotated dataset (e.g., MASS, Sleep-EDF with multiple scorers); testable by simulating label noise at known rates and measuring conformal coverage degradation.

mechanism_variables: Activity type (rest, walk, run, bike, etc.) from accelerometer classification
Activity intensity (METs or vector magnitude counts/min)
Cardiovascular dynamics metrics (HR turbulence, BP variability, pulse transit time)
Sensor noise metrics (motion artifact power, SNR)
Residual distribution parameters per activity stratum
mechanism_builds.causal_path: Physical activity → altered cardiovascular dynamics (HR turbulence, BP variability) + increased sensor noise → distinct residual regimes per activity → unstratified calibration mixes regimes → empirical quantile reflects mixture distribution → intervals too narrow for high-dynamic states (exercise) → systematic undercoverage during exercise
mechanism_builds.expected_direction: Undercoverage ≥ 15% at nominal 90% during vigorous activity (METs > 6) when calibrated on mixed/rest data; overcoverage ≥ 5% during rest if calibration dominated by exercise; activity-stratified calibration restores nominal coverage per stratum
domain_specific_boundary_conditions: Free-living monitoring with diverse activities (rest to vigorous)
Activity context unobserved or not used for stratified conformal prediction
Residual variance during exercise ≥ 3× rest variance
Sufficient samples per activity for stratified calibration (≥ 100 segments)
measurable_outcomes: Coverage per activity type/intensity bin
Coverage deviation vs. METs (continuous)
Minimum activity stratification granularity (number of strata) for nominal coverage
Calibration quantile shift when adding activity as stratification variable
mechanism_builds.mechanism_builder_notes: Testable on datasets with synchronized accelerometer and physiological signals (e.g., PPG-DaLiA, WESAD, Apple Watch studies); compare unstratified vs. activity-stratified conformal prediction.

mechanism_variables: Unmeasured confounder proxies: hydration (urine specific gravity, bioimpedance), medication timing (hours since dose), caffeine/alcohol intake (self-report)
Measured covariates (age, sex, BMI, activity, time-of-day)
Segment/session indicator
Residual values and conformity scores
Confounder distribution shift magnitude across segments (e.g., KL divergence)
mechanism_builds.causal_path: Unobserved confounders (hydration, medication, caffeine) → simultaneous influence on physiological signal (e.g., HRV, BP) and prediction target → segment-wise residual dependencies conditional on observed covariates → marginal conformal coverage guarantee does not protect against conditional coverage failure → coverage varies with confounder distribution across segments
mechanism_builds.expected_direction: Coverage deviation correlates with confounder distribution shift magnitude (e.g., |coverage - nominal| > 0.05 when KL divergence of hydration distribution > 0.5); segments with medication-on vs. medication-off show ≥ 10% coverage gap
domain_specific_boundary_conditions: Key confounders vary systematically across recording sessions/segments
Confounders not captured in feature set (no medication logs, hydration measures)
Exchangeability violated conditional on observed covariates
No randomized intervention to break confounding
measurable_outcomes: Coverage vs. proxy confounder measures (binned)
Sensitivity analysis bounds (e.g., Γ-value for hidden bias)
Residual correlation with unmeasured factors in subset with proxy data
Conditional coverage given observed covariates vs. marginal coverage gap
mechanism_builds.mechanism_builder_notes: Requires dataset with measured confounders (e.g., medication timestamps, hydration markers) to simulate hidden confounding; testable via sensitivity analysis (Rosenbaum bounds) on conformal coverage.

mechanism_variables: Effective sampling rate per segment (Hz)
Missing data rate (%) and pattern (burst vs. random)
Missingness mechanism classification (MCAR/MAR/MNAR via Little's test)
Imputation method (linear, spline, model-based) or downsampling factor
Residual distribution parameters and conformity score quantile per segment
mechanism_builds.causal_path: Non-random missingness correlated with signal quality (e.g., Bluetooth dropout during motion) → selection bias in observed calibration residuals → imputation/downsampling alters residual distributions differently across segments (distortion depends on missingness pattern) → conformity score distribution shifts across segments → coverage instability
mechanism_builds.expected_direction: Segments with MNAR missingness > 20% show coverage deviation ≥ 10% from nominal; direction depends on imputation bias (e.g., linear interpolation underestimates variability → overcoverage); MCAR missingness ≤ 30% maintains nominal coverage
domain_specific_boundary_conditions: Wearable sensors with Bluetooth/wireless transmission (dropout-prone)
Missingness correlated with motion/physiological state (MNAR)
Irregular sampling rates across segments/devices
No missing-data-aware conformal method (e.g., weighted conformal)
measurable_outcomes: Coverage vs. missing data rate (binned by mechanism: MCAR/MAR/MNAR)
Coverage vs. effective sampling rate
Bias in conformity score quantile under different imputation methods
Coverage when using missingness-aware vs. standard conformal prediction
mechanism_builds.mechanism_builder_notes: Testable by artificially introducing controlled missingness patterns (MCAR/MAR/MNAR) into complete physiological datasets and measuring conformal coverage degradation across imputation strategies.

mechanism_variables: Segment length (number of calibration samples n_seg)
Model effective degrees of freedom (DoF) or complexity measure (e.g., number of parameters, Rademacher complexity)
Conformity score empirical quantile estimation error (bootstrap SE)
Nominal coverage level (1-α)
Empirical coverage per segment
mechanism_builds.causal_path: Short segment length relative to model complexity → high-variance empirical quantile of conformity scores (finite-sample effect) → noisy coverage estimate per segment → segment-length-dependent coverage instability → variance of coverage across segments increases as n_seg/DoF decreases → worst for complex models (high DoF) on short segments
mechanism_builds.expected_direction: Coverage standard deviation across segments scales as √(DoF / n_seg); segments with n_seg/DoF < 10 show coverage variance ≥ 0.02² at nominal 90%; bias toward undercoverage for shortest segments due to quantile estimation bias
domain_specific_boundary_conditions: Segment lengths vary substantially (e.g., event-triggered recordings: 30s to 30min)
Model complexity high relative to shortest segments (DoF > n_min/5)
Finite calibration set (no asymptotic regime)
No pooling or hierarchical modeling across segments
measurable_outcomes: Coverage variance across segments vs. n_seg/DoF ratio
Coverage bias (mean - nominal) vs. segment length
Minimum n_seg for coverage variance < 0.01² at given DoF
Coverage improvement with hierarchical/Bayesian conformal methods
mechanism_builds.mechanism_builder_notes: Testable by subsampling calibration segments to varying lengths and measuring coverage distribution; compare fixed-window vs. adaptive conformal methods on heterogeneous segment lengths.

mechanism_variables: Pulse wave morphology features: augmentation index (AIx), pulse wave velocity (PWV), systolic/diastolic peak ratio, waveform entropy
Vascular tone indicators: mean arterial pressure, arterial stiffness index
Model prediction error (residual) per beat/segment
Morphology distribution shift metric (e.g., Wasserstein distance between calibration and test morphology features)
Segment-wise coverage
mechanism_builds.causal_path: Model misspecification (e.g., BP from PPG using fixed transfer function) → systematic error dependent on pulse wave morphology → morphology changes across segments due to vascular tone, aging, pathology → residual distribution shifts with morphology distribution → conformal calibration on one morphology distribution fails on shifted distribution → coverage breaks
mechanism_builds.expected_direction: Coverage deviation correlates with morphology distribution shift magnitude (Wasserstein distance > 0.5 → |coverage - nominal| > 0.08); segments with morphology features outside calibration convex hull show undercoverage ≥ 15%; including morphology as covariate in stratified conformal prediction restores nominal coverage
domain_specific_boundary_conditions: Predictive model for hemodynamic target from waveform (e.g., cuffless BP from PPG)
Model error depends on morphology features not included as covariates
Morphology varies across segments (vasodilation/constriction, pathology, aging)
Calibration morphology distribution differs from test deployment distribution
measurable_outcomes: Coverage vs. morphology distribution shift (Wasserstein distance bins)
Residual error vs. morphology features (AIx, PWV) regression
Coverage when adding morphology features to conformal stratification
Calibration quantile shift per morphology cluster
mechanism_builds.mechanism_builder_notes: Testable on cuffless BP datasets with simultaneous PPG and tonometry (e.g., MIMIC, VitalDB, or dedicated calibration studies); induce morphology shifts via vascular interventions (cold pressor, nitroglycerin) or compare young vs. old cohorts.
